en: The Verses on Pleasing Beings composed by the noble Nāgārjuna:
"It is solely for the sake of beings that I remain; it is through beings' faith [that I abide]."
She is not found elsewhere;
for alas, I have taken up the burden of sentient beings! That conduct which is devoid of compassion would be the lowest of practices.
Its abandonment is considered possible through compassion alone. ||1||
He whose activity toward sentient beings is characterized by intense compassion is one who honors me and knows the essential points of my teaching; for him,
ethical discipline, scriptural learning, compassion, and wisdom are present.
He alone is said to be one who constantly performs worship of the Sugata. || 2 ||
For the sake of performing what is virtuous, I have attained perfection;
I bear this very body solely for the benefit of sentient beings.
If I were not to act thus for the welfare of beings, [it would be in vain].
I make the nourishment of my body with food and drink utterly futile.
For how can he who harms sentient beings even in his mind take refuge in me alone, being indifferent toward me? Yet,
that very act becomes an offering if it is directed toward the welfare of sentient beings.
That which brings satisfaction to the mind of the one worthy of worship. || 4 ||
Worship that is violent in nature or arises from the harassment of others does not accord with the object of worship, even if it is refined.
[Such is the case with] wives, sons, wealth, greatness, and sovereignty.
And it carries the flesh, blood, and fat to the body. || 5 ||
Those for whose sake I have renounced that which is dear to me—
if anyone harms them, by him I am harmed;
for service to sentient beings is my supreme worship.
And through being intent on harming sentient beings, there would be defeat. || 6 ||
Having encountered sentient beings, I have performed virtuous deeds and propitiated the Protectors;
I have attained the perfections while remaining dedicated solely to the welfare of the assembly of sentient beings.
With a mind exerted for the sake of sentient beings, the power of Māra was shattered.
It was by sentient beings alone, through such and such arrangements, that I was made into a Buddha. || 7 ||
Upon what object can compassion and loving-kindness be established here? Upon what can they take their support?
What is the objective domain for equanimity, sympathetic joy, and the rest? In what are the liberations and so forth to be found?
For whose sake has patience been cultivated for a long time by one whose mind is devoted to compassion?
If living beings were not friends in the performance of pleasant deeds throughout birth after birth, they would not exist [as such]. (8)
It is sentient beings alone who have taken on the forms of elephants and other such states, whom I have given away many times;
it is sentient beings alone who have become worthy recipients, from whom I have accepted gifts.
It is through sentient beings alone, by their passage through various states of existence, that my compassion has been increased.
If I do not protect sentient beings themselves, for whose sake has this purpose been accomplished? (9)
If living beings were not made familiar with the world of Yama through the mockery of the whirlpools of birth in this saṃsāra, which abounds in calamities and blows,
then this marvelous and great majesty of the Sugata’s teaching— this crossing over from saṃsāra— would not exist.
For whose sake would there be any striving, if sentient beings were not dear to me? (10)
As long as this teaching of mine, which illuminates the world, endures, so long must you— who are self-possessed and devoted to the welfare of others— remain,
tirelessly hearing and internalizing what I have composed for the sake of sentient beings.
You should not feel weary, nor should you disregard this body which has been freed from its essence. || 11 ||
The Verses on Pleasing Sentient Beings, spoken by the Perfectly Enlightened One, are completed.
